claim: T4 dendrites reside in layer 10 of the medulla and compute the direction of moving bright edges (ON-pathway).
source: T4 dendrites reside in layer 10 of the medulla and compute the direction of moving bright edges (ON-pathway).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and is supported by citations to previous work (Maisak et al., 2013).

claim: T5 dendrites arborize in layer 1 of the lobula and compute the direction of moving dark edges (OFF-pathway).
source: T5 dendrites arborize in layer 1 of the lobula and compute the direction of moving dark edges (OFF-pathway) (Maisak et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with citation to Maisak et al., 2013.

claim: The four subtypes of T4/T5 neurons (a, b, c, d) project axon terminals to one of the four layers in the lobula plate, each responding only to movement in one of the four cardinal directions.
source: The four subtypes of T4/T5 neurons (a, b, c, d), project axon terminals to one of the four layers in the lobula plate, each responding only to movement in one of the four cardinal directions, their preferred direction (Maisak et al., 2013).
evidence: This is directly stated in the text with citation to Maisak et al., 2013.

claim: Glutamate can have inhibitory effects in invertebrates when it acts on a glutamate-gated chloride channel, known as GluClα.
source: Glutamate for instance is mainly excitatory, however, in invertebrates it can also have inhibitory effects when it acts on a glutamate-gated chloride channel, known as GluClα (Cully et al., 1996; Liu and Wilson, 2013; Mauss et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with citations to Cully et al., 1996; Liu and Wilson, 2013; Mauss et al., 2015.

claim: Acetylcholine might be inhibitory in Drosophila if it binds to the muscarinic mAChR-A receptor.
source: Recently, it has also been shown that acetylcholine, usually excitatory, might also be inhibitory in Drosophila, if it binds to the muscarinic mAChR-A receptor (Bielopolski et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with citation to Bielopolski et al., 2019.

claim: The voltage-gated calcium channel cacophony mediates influx of calcium ions that drives synaptic vesicle fusion at presynaptic sites.
source: The voltage-gated calcium channel cacophony, for instance, mediates influx of calcium ions that drives synaptic vesicle fusion at presynaptic sites (Kawasaki et al., 2004; Fisher et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with citations to Kawasaki et al., 2004; Fisher et al., 2017.

claim: Voltage-gated sodium channels like paralytic (para) are important for the cell's excitability and the generation of sodium-dependent action potentials.
source: Voltage-gated sodium channels like paralytic (para) are important for the cell's excitability and the generation of sodium-dependent action potentials.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and represents established knowledge about sodium channels.

claim: The voltage-gated channel Ih influences the integration and kinetics of excitatory postsynaptic potentials.
source: The voltage-gated channel Ih influences the integration and kinetics of excitatory postsynaptic potentials (Magee, 1999; Littleton and Ganetzky, 2000; George et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with citations to Magee, 1999; Littleton and Ganetzky, 2000; George et al., 2009.

claim: T4 dendrites receive input from the glutamatergic medulla neuron Mi9.
source: As suggested by the connectome (Takemura et al., 2017; Shinomiya et al., 2019) and antibody staining against the vesicular glutamate transporter VGluT (Richter et al., 2018), T4 cells receive input on their dendrites from the glutamatergic medulla neuron Mi9.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with citations to Takemura et al., 2017; Shinomiya et al., 2019; Richter et al., 2018.

claim: GluClα is the most highly expressed glutamate receptor in T4 neurons.
source: According to a RNA-sequencing study, GluClα is the most highly expressed glutamate receptor in T4 neurons (Davis et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with citation to Davis et al., 2020.

claim: GluClα is found in T4 dendrites of the medulla, distributed in discrete puncta arranged in circular clusters corresponding to columns.
source: We found GluClα in T4 dendrites of the medulla, where it is distributed in discrete puncta (Figure 2A; horizontal section, first two panels). A top view of the medulla of these flies reveals that these puncta are arranged in circular clusters, each corresponding to one column (Figure 2A, right panel).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: T5 dendrites are completely devoid of GluClα signal.
source: Conversely, T5 dendrites are completely devoid of GluClα signal (Figure 2A, first two panels).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Mi9 is the only glutamatergic presynaptic partner of T4 cells in the medulla.
source: Since Mi9 is the only glutamatergic presynaptic partner of T4 cells in the medulla (Takemura et al., 2017; Richter et al., 2018; Shinomiya et al., 2019), this columnar arrangement likely reflects the columnar array of Mi9 cell inputs.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with citations to Takemura et al., 2017; Richter et al., 2018; Shinomiya et al., 2019.

claim: GFP signal of GluClα::GFP is visible in the axon terminals of T4/T5 in the lobula plate.
source: In addition to the medulla layer 10, GFP signal of GluClα::GFP is also visible in the axon terminals of T4/T5 in the lobula plate (Figure 2A, first two panels).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Both T4 and T5 neurons express the glutamate receptor GluClα in their axon terminals in the lobula plate.
source: Interestingly, with these specific driver lines, both T4 and T5 neurons express the glutamate receptor in their axon terminals in the lobula plate (Figure 2B and Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figures 2B and 2C.

claim: GluClα was predominantly localized to the distal tips of individual T4 dendrites across all four T4 subtypes.
source: In individual T4 dendrites, we observed that GluClα was predominantly localized to the distal tips, which holds true for all four T4 subtypes (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The number of GluClα-puncta per T4 cell dendrite (mean: 20.5 puncta) matches closely the number of glutamatergic input synapses made by Mi9 onto one T4 cell (mean: 23 synaptic contacts).
source: The number of GluClα-puncta per T4 cell dendrite (mean: 20.5 puncta) matches closely the number of glutamatergic input synapses made by Mi9 onto one T4 cell (mean: 23 synaptic contacts; personal communication, K. Shinomiya, May 2020) (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is stated in the text with reference to EM data and shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Every GluClα-punctum resolved by confocal microscopy in individually labeled T4 dendrites represents one postsynaptic GluClα receptor cluster corresponding to one Mi9-T4 synapse.
source: This suggests that every GluClα-punctum resolved by confocal microscopy in individually labeled T4 dendrites represents one postsynaptic GluClα receptor cluster corresponding to one Mi9-T4 synapse.
evidence: This is an inference based on the matching numbers of puncta and synapses.

claim: T4 dendrites receive input from several GABAergic cell-types in the medulla: Mi4, C3, CT1, and TmY15.
source: T4 dendrites receive input from several GABAergic cell-types in the medulla: on the proximal base of the dendrite, these are the columnar cells Mi4, C3; the multicolumnar amacrine cell CT1 in the middle and distal part of the dendrite as well as TmY15 (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: T5 dendrites receive GABAergic input from only two cell-types: CT1 on the proximal base and TmY15 throughout the central and distal area of the dendrite.
source: In contrast, T5 dendrites receive GABAergic input from only two cell-types: CT1 on the proximal base and TmY15 again throughout the central and distal area of the dendrite (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Rdl is the most highly expressed ionotropic GABA receptor subunit in T4 and T5 neurons.
source: We focused on the GABA receptor subunit Rdl, since RNA-sequencing studies had identified Rdl as the most highly expressed ionotropic GABA receptor subunit in T4 and T5 neurons (Pankova and Borst, 2016; Davis et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with citations to Pankova and Borst, 2016; Davis et al., 2020.

claim: Five Rdl subunits can form a homomeric chloride channel which leads to hyperpolarization upon GABA-binding.
source: Five Rdl subunits can form a homomeric chloride channel which leads to hyperpolarization upon GABA-binding, thus representing a receptor (Ffrench-Constant et al., 1993).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with citation to Ffrench-Constant et al., 1993.

claim: Rdl is expressed in both T4/T5 dendrites, but not in the axon terminals.
source: Combining this line with a T4/T5 specific Gal4-line and a membrane-bound tdTomato revealed Rdl expression in both T4/T5 dendrites, but not in the axon terminals (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Rdl is found on the proximal base and in the central area of both T4 and T5 dendrites across all four subtypes.
source: We found Rdl on the proximal base and in the central area of both T4 and T5 dendrites across all four subtypes (Figure 3B and Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figures 3B and 3C.

claim: The numbers of Rdl receptor clusters in T4 and T5 dendrites (roughly 40 receptor clusters) match the sum of all GABAergic input synapses to T4 (mean: 40.45) and T5 (mean: 37).
source: We found similar numbers of roughly 40 receptor clusters for both T4 and T5 which match the sum of all GABAergic input synapses to T4 (mean: 40.45) and T5 (mean: 37) (Figure 3E) (EM numbers: personal communication, K. Shinomiya, May 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the text with reference to EM data and shown in Figure 3E.

claim: T4 dendrites receive most of their input synapses from cholinergic Mi1 and Tm3 cells at the center of their dendrite.
source: According to connectome data, T4 dendrites receive most of their input synapses from cholinergic Mi1 and Tm3 cells at the center of their dendrite (Takemura et al., 2017; Shinomiya et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with citations to Takemura et al., 2017; Shinomiya et al., 2019.

claim: T4 neurons of the same subtype form synapses with each other at the distal tips of their dendrites.
source: Furthermore, T4 neurons of the same subtype form synapses with each other at the distal tips of their dendrites (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: T4-T4 synapses are thought to be cholinergic.
source: As T4 neurons are cholinergic (Mauss et al., 2014; Davis et al., 2020), these T4-T4 synapses are thought to be cholinergic as well.
evidence: This is an inference based on T4 neurons being cholinergic, with citations to Mauss et al., 2014; Davis et al., 2020.

claim: T5 dendrites receive cholinergic input from Tm1, Tm2, and Tm4 in the central area of the dendrite.
source: With the exception of GABAergic CT1, T5 dendrites receive cholinergic input from Tm1, Tm2, and Tm4 in the central area of the dendrite.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text.

claim: Tm9 and T5 provide cholinergic input mainly towards the distal tips of the T5 dendrite.
source: Tm9 and T5 provide cholinergic input mainly towards the distal tips of the dendrite (Figure 1D; Takemura et al., 2017; Shinomiya et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to Takemura et al., 2017; Shinomiya et al., 2019 and shown in Figure 1D.

claim: T5 dendrites receive almost twice as many cholinergic inputs as T4; 160 and 87 synapses, respectively.
source: T5 dendrites receive almost twice as many cholinergic inputs as T4; 160 and 87 synapses, respectively (Shinomiya et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with citation to Shinomiya et al., 2019.

claim: Dα7 is one of 10 different nicotinic ACh receptor subunits found in the Drosophila genome.
source: Dα7 is one of 10 different nicotinic ACh receptor subunits (Dα1-Dα7 and Dß1-Dß3) found in the Drosophila genome.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and represents established knowledge.

claim: Dα5, Dα6, and Dα7 can form homomeric ACh receptors.
source: In addition, Dα5, Dα6, and Dα7 can also form homomeric ACh receptors (Lansdell and Millar, 2004; Lansdell et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with citations to Lansdell and Millar, 2004; Lansdell et al., 2012.

claim: Both T4 and T5 neurons express almost every ACh receptor subunit, except for Dα6 and Dß3.
source: According to RNA-sequencing data, both T4 and T5 neurons express almost every ACh receptor subunit, except for Dα6 and Dß3 (Davis et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with citation to Davis et al., 2020.

claim: Dα7 is distributed to both T4 and T5 dendrites while their axon terminals remained devoid.
source: Expression of UAS-Dα7::GFP with a T4/T5-Gal4 line, revealed the distribution of Dα7 to both T4 and T5 dendrites while their axon terminals remained devoid (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Overexpressed Dα7::GFP localizes to cholinergic synapses and becomes part of an ACh-receptor, even if this subtype is not endogenously expressed in this neuron.
source: This suggests that overexpressed Dα7::GFP localizes to cholinergic synapses and becomes part of an ACh-receptor, even if this subtype is not endogenously expressed in this neuron.
evidence: This is an inference based on the Mi1 overexpression experiment.

claim: Dα7 was distributed along the central area and distal tips of both T4 and T5 dendrites whereas the proximal base of the dendrite was completely devoid of Dα7 signal.
source: Dα7 was distributed along the central area and distal tips of both T4 and T5 dendrites whereas the proximal base of the dendrite was completely devoid of Dα7 signal (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figures 4B and 4C.

claim: For T4 dendrites the numbers of Dα7 puncta quantified (mean: 88.4) matched the numbers of cholinergic input synapses mapped by EM reconstruction (mean: 86.9).
source: For T4 dendrites the numbers of Dα7 puncta quantified (mean: 88.4) matched the numbers of cholinergic input synapses mapped by EM reconstruction (mean: 86.9; personal communication, K. Shinomiya, May 2020) (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is stated in the text with reference to EM data and shown in Figure 4E.

claim: For T5 dendrites the Dα7 puncta exhibited 60 synapses less on average when compared to the mean of the summed cholinergic EM input synapse.
source: However, for T5 dendrites the Dα7 puncta exhibited 60 synapses less on average when compared to the mean of the summed cholinergic EM input synapse (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The FlpTag cassette is a protein trap cassette consisting of a central GFP tag placed between a splice acceptor (SA) and splice donor (SD), flanked by specific Frt sites forming a FLEX-switch for stable inversion.
source: The FlpTag cassette is a protein trap cassette consisting of a central GFP tag placed between a splice acceptor (SA) and splice donor (SD), flanked by specific Frt sites forming a FLEX-switch for stable inversion (Figure 5A, upper panel) (Schnütgen et al., 2003; Xue et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to Schnütgen et al., 2003; Xue et al., 2014 and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The FlpTag cassette is integrated into an intronic coding region of interest by recombinase mediate cassette exchange (RMCE) in vivo.
source: The FlpTag cassette is integrated into an intronic coding region of interest by recombinase mediate cassette exchange (RMCE) in vivo.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text.

claim: The distribution pattern of GluClα seen with the FlpTag line is virtually identical to the UAS-GluClα::GFP genotype.
source: The distribution pattern of GluClα seen here is virtually identical to the UAS-GluClα::GFP genotype: GluClα is localized to T4 dendrites, the T5 dendrite area is devoid of GluClα signal, and T4/T5 axon terminals in the lobula plate co-localize with GluClα (Figure 5B, compare with Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown by comparing Figures 5B and 2A.

claim: The metabotropic GABA receptor subunit Gaba-b-r1 is the most highly expressed GABA receptor subunit in T4/T5 neurons after Rdl.
source: The metabotropic GABA receptor subunit Gaba-b-r1 is the most highly expressed GABA receptor subunit in T4/T5 neurons after Rdl (Pankova and Borst, 2016; Davis et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with citations to Pankova and Borst, 2016; Davis et al., 2020.

claim: Gaba-b-r1 is one out of three G-protein-coupled GABA receptor subunits described in Drosophila.
source: Gaba-b-r1 is one out of three G-protein-coupled GABA receptor subunits described in Drosophila and has been shown to be involved in sleep and appetitive long-term memory (Mezler et al., 2001; Kim et al., 2017; Pavlowsky et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with citations to Mezler et al., 2001; Kim et al., 2017; Pavlowsky et al., 2018.

claim: No Gaba-b-r1::GFP signal was observed in T4/T5 dendrites or axons upon cell-type specific, FLP-dependent inversion of the FlpTag cassette in T4/T5 neurons.
source: Upon cell-type specific, FLP-dependent inversion of the FlpTag cassette in T4/T5 neurons, we could not observe any Gaba-b-r1::GFP signal in T4/T5 dendrites or axons (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Paralytic (para) is the only voltage-gated sodium channel described in Drosophila and highly expressed in T4/T5 neurons.
source: Paralytic (para) is the only voltage-gated sodium channel described in Drosophila and highly expressed in T4/T5 neurons (Pankova and Borst, 2016).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with citation to Pankova and Borst, 2016.

claim: Para is required for the generation of sodium-dependent action potentials.
source: It is required for the generation of sodium-dependent action potentials.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and represents established knowledge about para.

claim: In the T4/T5 specific FlpTag genotype, para is strongly expressed in the axonal fibers connecting dendrites and axon terminals in T4/T5 neurons.
source: In the T4/T5 specific FlpTag genotype, para is strongly expressed in the axonal fibers connecting dendrites and axon terminals in T4/T5 neurons (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Ih is a voltage-gated, hyperpolarization-activated ion channel which is highly expressed in T4/T5 neurons.
source: Ih is a voltage-gated, hyperpolarization-activated ion channel which is highly expressed in T4/T5 neurons (Chen and Wang, 2012; Hu et al., 2015; Pankova and Borst, 2016).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with citations to Chen and Wang, 2012; Hu et al., 2015; Pankova and Borst, 2016.

claim: In the T4/T5-specific FlpTag genotype, Ih is localized to the T4 and T5 dendrite area in medulla layer 10 and lobula plate layer 1.
source: In the T4/T5-specific FlpTag genotype, Ih is localized to the T4 and T5 dendrite area in medulla layer 10 and lobula plate layer 1 (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6F.

claim: The receptor subunits GluClα, Rdl, and Dα7 reveal a distinct distribution profile along the dendrites of individual T4/T5 cells that can be assigned to specific input neurons forming synapses in this area.
source: Along the dendrites of individual T4/T5 cells, the receptor subunits GluClα, Rdl, and Dα7 reveal a distinct distribution profile that can be assigned to specific input neurons forming synapses in this area.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and is a summary of the findings.

claim: The subcellular distribution of GluClα, Rdl and Dα7 matched the previously reported EM-reconstructed synapse distributions.
source: We discovered a strictly segregated subcellular distribution of these proteins and a sequential spatial arrangement of glutamate, acetylcholine, and GABA receptors along the dendrite that matched the previously reported EM-reconstructed synapse distributions.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and represents a key finding of the study.

claim: T4/T5 dendrites span around eight columns collecting signals from several presynaptic input neurons, each of which samples information from visual space in a retinotopic manner.
source: Both T4 and T5 dendrites span around eight columns collecting signals from several presynaptic input neurons, each of which samples information from visual space in a retinotopic manner (Haag et al., 2016; Shinomiya et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with citations to Haag et al., 2016; Shinomiya et al., 2019.

claim: T4 dendrites receive glutamatergic, GABAergic and cholinergic input.
source: T4 dendrites receive glutamatergic, GABAergic and cholinergic input, whereas T5 dendrites receive GABAergic and cholinergic input only.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text.

claim: T5 dendrites receive GABAergic and cholinergic input only.
source: T4 dendrites receive glutamatergic, GABAergic and cholinergic input, whereas T5 dendrites receive GABAergic and cholinergic input only.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text.

claim: Input synapses to T4/T5 are arranged in a specific spatial order along T4/T5 dendrites.
source: These input synapses are arranged in a specific spatial order along T4/T5 dendrites (s. Figure 1C and D; for overview Takemura et al., 2017; Shinomiya et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to Takemura et al., 2017; Shinomiya et al., 2019 and shown in Figures 1C and D.

claim: mRNA and protein levels are regulated in complex ways via post-transcriptional, translational, and protein degradation mechanisms making it difficult to assign protein levels to RNA levels.
source: However, RNA-sequencing studies do not unambiguously answer the above question for two reasons: mRNA and protein levels are regulated in complex ways via post-transcriptional, translational, and protein degradation mechanisms making it difficult to assign protein levels to RNA levels (Vogel and Marcotte, 2012).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with citation to Vogel and Marcotte, 2012.

claim: Standard RNA-sequencing techniques cannot provide spatial information about receptor localizations.
source: Secondly, standard RNA-sequencing techniques cannot provide spatial information about receptor localizations, hence, they are not sufficient to conclude which transmitter receptors receive which input signal.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text.

claim: At an algorithmic level, a three-arm detector model is sufficient to describe how direction-selective responses in T4/T5 neurons arise.
source: At an algorithmic level, a three-arm detector model is sufficient to describe how direction-selective responses in T4/T5 neurons arise (Arenz et al., 2017; Haag et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with citations to Arenz et al., 2017; Haag et al., 2017.

claim: The three-arm detector model relies on the comparison of signals originating from three neighboring points in space via a delay-and-compare mechanism.
source: This model relies on the comparison of signals originating from three neighboring points in space via a delay-and-compare mechanism.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text.

claim: Mi9 has an OFF-center receptive field.
source: However, since Mi9 has an OFF-center receptive field (Arenz et al., 2017; Richter et al., 2018; Drews et al., 2020), this glutamatergic synapse will invert the polarity from Mi9-OFF to T4-ON.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with citations to Arenz et al., 2017; Richter et al., 2018; Drews et al., 2020.

claim: The RNAi-knock-down of GluClα in T4/T5 neurons leads to enhanced turning responses on the ball set-up for faster speeds of repeating ON and OFF edges.
source: Nevertheless, Strother et al. showed that the RNAi- knock-down of GluClα in T4/T5 neurons leads to enhanced turning responses on the ball set-up for faster speeds of repeating ON and OFF edges (Strother et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with citation to Strother et al., 2017.

claim: Glutamatergic LPi neurons receive a cholinergic, excitatory signal from T4/T5 neurons within one layer and inhibit lobula plate tangential cells via GluClα in the adjacent oppositely tuned layer.
source: Glutamatergic LPi neurons are known to receive a cholinergic, excitatory signal from T4/T5 neurons within one layer and to inhibit lobula plate tangential cells, the downstream postsynaptic partners of T4/T5 neurons, via GluClα in the adjacent oppositely tuned layer.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text.

claim: This mechanism induces a motion opponent response in lobula plate tangential cells and increases their flow-field selectivity.
source: This mechanism induces a motion opponent response in lobula plate tangential cells and increases their flow-field selectivity (Mauss et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with citation to Mauss et al., 2015.

claim: Inhibition via GABA plays an essential role in creating direction-selective responses in both T4 and T5 neurons by providing null direction suppression.
source: Third, inhibition via GABA plays an essential role in creating direction-selective responses in both T4 and T5 neurons (Fisher et al., 2015a; Arenz et al., 2017; Strother et al., 2017; Gruntman et al., 2018) by providing null direction suppression.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with citations to Fisher et al., 2015a; Arenz et al., 2017; Strother et al., 2017; Gruntman et al., 2018.

claim: Computer simulations showed that direction selectivity decreases in T4/T5 motion detector models without inhibitory input on the null side of the dendrite.
source: Computer simulations showed that direction selectivity decreases in T4/T5 motion detector models without this inhibitory input on the null side of the dendrite (Arenz et al., 2017; Borst, 2018; Strother et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with citations to Arenz et al., 2017; Borst, 2018; Strother et al., 2017.

claim: All of the receptor subunits GluClα, Rdl and Dα7 investigated are ionotropic, fast receptors.
source: Finally, all of the receptor subunits GluClα, Rdl and Dα7 investigated here are ionotropic, fast receptors, which presumably do not add a temporal delay at the synaptic level.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text.

claim: Ih channels are activated at negative potentials below −50 mV.
source: Ih channels are activated at negative potentials below −50 mV and as they are permeable to sodium and potassium ions, they can cause a depolarization of the cell after hyperpolarization (Magee, 1999; Littleton and Ganetzky, 2000; George et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with citations to Magee, 1999; Littleton and Ganetzky, 2000; George et al., 2009.

claim: There are MiMIC insertions in coding introns for more than 2800 genes available, which covers approximately 24% of neuronal genes.
source: As of now, there are MiMIC insertions in coding introns for more than 2800 genes available, which covers approximately 24% of neuronal genes (Venken et al., 2011; Nagarkar-Jaiswal et al., 2015a; Fisher et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with citations to Venken et al., 2011; Nagarkar-Jaiswal et al., 2015a; Fisher et al., 2017.

claim: The FlpTag approach is generalizable and can be expanded to many genes with MiMIC insertion sites.
source: We demonstrated that the FlpTag approach is generalizable and can be expanded to many genes with MiMIC insertion sites.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and is a key conclusion of the study.

claim: Overexpression of GFP-tagged GluClα, introduced as a transgene, leads to a subcellular localization pattern that seems to be identical to the endogenous GluClα protein.
source: Hence, overexpression of GFP-tagged GluClα, introduced as a transgene, leads to a subcellular localization pattern that seems to be identical to the endogenous GluClα protein.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and is based on comparison with MiMIC and FlpTag lines.

claim: The UAS-Dα7::GFP line cannot be used to define the exact composition of ACh receptor subunits of cholinergic synapses, but labels (nicotinic) ACh receptors in general.
source: Hence, the UAS-Dα7::GFP line can be used to study the distribution of cholinergic synapses, but not the exact composition of cholinergic receptor subunits.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and is based on the Mi1 overexpression experiment.

claim: Rdl is not expressed in the lamina monopolar neuron L1.
source: According to RNA-sequencing, Rdl is not expressed in the lamina monopolar neuron L1 (Davis et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with citation to Davis et al., 2020.

claim: When UAS-Rdl::GFP was overexpressed by means of a L1-Gal4 driver line, Rdl signal is not detectable in L1 dendrites.
source: When we overexpressed UAS-Rdl::GFP by means of a L1-Gal4 driver line, Rdl signal is not detectable in L1 dendrites (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Overexpressed Rdl only localizes to endogenous GABA synapses that are composed of the Rdl subunit.
source: This suggests that overexpressed Rdl only localizes to endogenous GABA synapses that are composed of the Rdl subunit.
evidence: This is an inference based on the L1 overexpression experiment.

claim: Dα7 is not expressed in Mi1.
source: Transcriptomic data revealed that Dα7 is not expressed in Mi1 (Davis et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with citation to Davis et al., 2020.

claim: Mi1 receives cholinergic input from L3 and L5 and expresses several different ACh receptor subunits.
source: However, Mi1 receives cholinergic input from L3 and L5 and expresses several different ACh receptor subunits (Takemura et al., 2017; Shinomiya et al., 2019; Davis et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with citations to Takemura et al., 2017; Shinomiya et al., 2019; Davis et al., 2020.

claim: When UAS-Dα7::GFP was overexpressed in Mi1, Dα7 localized to layers 1 and 5 of the medulla, where the dendrites of Mi1 neurons arborize and receive cholinergic input from L3 and L5.
source: When UAS-Dα7::GFP was overexpressed in Mi1, Dα7 localized to layers 1 and 5 of the medulla, where the dendrites of Mi1 neurons arborize and receive cholinergic input from L3 and L5 (Takemura et al., 2017; Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation to Takemura et al., 2017 and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The FlpTag cassette can be knocked-in into any desired locus through HDR.
source: Through HDR the FlpTag cassette can be knocked-in into any desired locus.
